payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_witness_gate.py::test_a_witness_that_fails_only_by_raising_reads_as_raised_and_moves_no_status stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The pattern is searched anywhere in the detail with `re.search`, so a detail naming the word later reads as an assertion.' applied to saffron/gates/core/witness.py as an edit. The claim was '`witness_gate` takes a keyword `assertion`, a pattern or `None`. A witness whose `tests` result under its edit is `fail` raised when the pattern is declared, the result holds at least one failure, and every failure\'s `detail` is non-empty and unmatched by `re.match` with the pattern. A raised witness is neither died nor survived. It moves no status: a gate whose only verdicts are raises reports `pass`, and raises add no failure to any result. The summary carries one clause naming every raised witness with its first failure\'s detail, joined by commas. The clause follows the died, survived or miscount count and comes ahead of the "not proven" note, whatever the status. The died count leaves raised witnesses out. The pattern alone decides what reads as an assertion, and core names no word of its own. A matched detail, an empty detail beside an unmatched one, one matched detail among unmatched ones, a `fail` with no failure and an undeclared pattern each read as died, as at base. A derived criterion is judged the same way as a declared one. The witness drives `witness_gate` directly with a stub mutator. A lone `KeyError` detail reads `pass` with no failure and the raised clause. Five kills and an undeclared pattern read the base summary. A detail that holds the matched word later in its text, beside a second unmatched detail, names its first detail. A kill beside two raises reads `pass`, counts one of three died and names both raises in one clause. A survivor beside a raise reads `fail` with only the survivor\'s failure and both clauses. A miscount beside a raise reads `fail` with only the miscount\'s failure and both clauses. An unproven criterion beside a raise puts the clause ahead of the note. A derived criterion that raises is named. Under the pattern `^KeyError\\b` a `KeyError` detail reads died and `assert 1 == 2` reads raised.', and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
